title: A short exact sequence of coherent formal modules is levelwise right exact, and the kernel levels are quotients of levelwise kernels
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] with quasi-compact underlying space) and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and let $0\to(\mathcal G_n)\xrightarrow{\beta}(\mathcal F_n)\xrightarrow{\alpha}(\mathcal H_n)\to0$ be a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] in the abelian category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module, lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian], with components $\beta_n:\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal F_n$ and $\alpha_n:\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal H_n$. Then: (a) for every $n\ge1$ the sequence $\mathcal G_n\xrightarrow{\beta_n}\mathcal F_n\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}\mathcal H_n\to0$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules is exact in the abelian category of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] (exact at $\mathcal F_n$, and $\alpha_n$ surjective); (b) for every $n\ge1$ there are an integer $m\ge n$ and a surjective $\mathcal O_X$-linear map from the $\mathcal O_X$-module $\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_m)\subseteq\mathcal F_m$ onto $\mathcal G_n$. (In general $\beta_n$ is not injective.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), remarks (a) and (b) of its first paragraph, which refer to the proof of Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian): cokernels are termwise, and the kernel of alpha has levels K_n = K'_m/I^n K'_m with K'_m the image of Ker(alpha_l) -> F_m for l >= m + c

proof.text: (Isomorphisms of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ and uniqueness of kernels and cokernels.) Composition in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is termwise [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (1), so if $\varphi=(\varphi_n)$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\psi=(\psi_n)$, then $\psi_n\circ\varphi_n=\mathrm{id}$ and $\varphi_n\circ\psi_n=\mathrm{id}$, i.e. every $\varphi_n$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. If $q:\mathcal F\to\mathcal C$ and $q':\mathcal F\to\mathcal C'$ are two cokernels of the same morphism $\beta$ of a category with zero morphisms, the universal properties give $\varphi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ and $\psi:\mathcal C'\to\mathcal C$ with $\varphi\circ q=q'$, $\psi\circ q'=q$; then $\psi\varphi q=q=\mathrm{id}\circ q$ and $\varphi\psi q'=q'$, so by the uniqueness clauses $\psi\varphi=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi\psi=\mathrm{id}$: $\varphi$ is an isomorphism with $\varphi\circ q=q'$. Dually, two kernels $\iota:\mathcal K\to\mathcal F$, $\iota':\mathcal K'\to\mathcal F$ of the same morphism differ by an isomorphism $\psi:\mathcal K\to\mathcal K'$ with $\iota'\circ\psi=\iota$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), first paragraph, remark (a); proof of Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian): the cokernel of alpha is (Coker alpha_n)

proof.text: (Proof of (a).) By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is abelian, and by the definition of a short exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] the complex $(\mathcal G_n)\xrightarrow{\beta}(\mathcal F_n)\xrightarrow{\alpha}(\mathcal H_n)$ is exact at $(\mathcal F_n)$ and $\alpha$ is an epimorphism; hence $\alpha$ is a cokernel of $\beta$ [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (a). By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] (cokernel clause; its proof constructs it as the system of the termwise cokernels with the termwise quotient maps) another cokernel of $\beta$ is $q=(q_n):(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal C_n)$, $q_n:\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal C_n=\operatorname{Coker}\beta_n$ the cokernel of $\beta_n$ in $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By Step 1 there is an isomorphism $\varphi:(\mathcal C_n)\to(\mathcal H_n)$ with $\alpha=\varphi\circ q$, and every $\varphi_n$ is an isomorphism, so $\alpha_n=\varphi_n\circ q_n$. The modules $\mathcal G_n,\mathcal F_n$ are coherent, hence quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (1) $q_n$ is an epimorphism with $\ker q_n=\operatorname{Im}\beta_n$. Therefore $\alpha_n$ is an epimorphism (surjective) and $\ker\alpha_n=\ker q_n=\operatorname{Im}\beta_n$ ($\varphi_n$ being injective), i.e. $\mathcal G_n\to\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal H_n\to0$ is exact for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0CYV (lemma-systems-with-proper-support), first paragraph, remark (a); proof of Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian): the cokernel of alpha is (Coker alpha_n)

proof.text: (Proof of (b).) Since $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is abelian [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] and the sequence is short exact, $\beta$ is a kernel of $\alpha$ [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-short-exact-kernel]. Let $c\ge0$, $\mathcal K'_{l,m}$, $\mathcal K'_m$, $\mathcal K_n=\mathcal K'_{n+c}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_{n+c}$ and $\iota:(\mathcal K_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)$ be as in [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module-kernel] for $\alpha$; $\iota$ is also a kernel of $\alpha$, so by Step 1 there is an isomorphism $\psi:(\mathcal K_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ with $\beta\circ\psi=\iota$, and each $\psi_n:\mathcal K_n\to\mathcal G_n$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Fix $n\ge1$ and put $m=n+2c\ge n$. As $m\ge(n+c)+c$, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module-kernel] (1) gives $\mathcal K'_{n+c}=\mathcal K'_{m,n+c}$, the image sheaf of $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_m\hookrightarrow\mathcal F_m\to\mathcal F_{n+c}$. The corestriction $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_m\to\mathcal K'_{n+c}$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear and surjective: by the definition of the image sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], every local section of $\mathcal K'_{n+c}$ is locally the image of a local section of $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_m$. The quotient map $\mathcal K'_{n+c}\to\mathcal K'_{n+c}/\mathcal I^n\mathcal K'_{n+c}=\mathcal K_n$ is a cokernel, hence surjective ([def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0), [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (1)), and $\psi_n$ is an isomorphism. The composite $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_m\to\mathcal K'_{n+c}\to\mathcal K_n\xrightarrow{\psi_n}\mathcal G_n$ is therefore a surjective $\mathcal O_X$-linear map, which is (b).

proof.text: (Remark: $\beta_n$ need not be injective.) Under the isomorphism $\psi$ of Step 3, $\beta_n\circ\psi_n=\iota_n$, and $\iota_n$ is not injective in general [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module-kernel] (3); this is why (a) asserts exactness only at $\mathcal F_n$ and $\mathcal H_n$.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks 0CYV (first paragraph) and 087X (proof). (a): alpha is a cokernel of beta (exact at F, alpha epi; lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel (a)); the abelian node gives the termwise cokernel; the two cokernels differ by an isomorphism with isomorphic components, so alpha_n = phi_n o q_n is surjective with kernel Im beta_n. (b): beta is a kernel of alpha (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-abelian-short-exact-kernel, ShortComplex.ShortExact.fIsKernel); the explicit kernel (K'_{n+c}/I^n K'_{n+c}) of 087X claims (a)-(d) is stated in the new node lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module-kernel, because the statement of lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian describes only cokernels (its Steps 3-6 prove the kernel description in its proof only); with m = n + 2c, Ker(alpha_m) -> K'_{n+c} -> K_n -> G_n is the required surjection. Added def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence to the statement (citation) and stmt_deps. The remark that beta_n need not be injective is justified by the kernel node.
